data.narrative:
ABL Bio is a public-stage biotech & health company (KOSDAQ-listed) founded by Sang Hoon Lee. The relevant peer universe comprises 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, Chai Discovery, New Limit, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Standard valuation triangulation methods face material constraints here. Peer-median multiples cannot be reliably applied: the 8 same-sector private peers lack sufficient overlap on stage, valuation tier, or business model to yield three or more meaningfully comparable datapoints. Public-comp anchoring is likewise inapplicable—while the Biotech & Health sector median P/S across the 3 public tickers stands at 6.6x, ABL Bio's revenue figure is not on file, precluding multiple-based extrapolation. The absence of revenue disclosure, typical for many private-stage biotech entities, eliminates this common pathway.

Given these constraints, a defensible valuation range cannot be triangulated from the available data. The analysis reveals a structural limitation: ABL Bio's public listing status and $5B+ cumulative fundraising (IPO plus licensing) suggest material scale, but the absence of disclosed revenue and a sufficiently granular peer set prevents quantitative anchoring. Further disclosure of revenue or comparable EBITDA metrics, or identification of narrower peer groupings by therapeutic focus or development stage, would be required to support a specific valuation range with confidence.
